text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing correlated latency spikes across multiple tenants on eu-west GPUs starting ~10:12UTC. traces show repeated slab throttling (kvcache eviction storms) and long tail in p99 gen latency. digging in now.

lina: ugh, that pattern again. can you paste the slab/queue histograms? suspect a single tenant is saturating NIC RX and causing head-of-line for host->gpu paths.

alex: histos attached (summary): slab-throttle-count +1200 in 3m window, RX-queue-depth spiked to 512, nvlink util normal. stack traces show heavy kvcache invalidation from model A/tenant-819.

kai: any chance this is a traffic amplification from batching? we had a recent canary that increased prefix cache joins. if so, routing to dedicated slices temporarily should help.

ben: also noticing our telemetry aggregator sample window is 30s — means we detect these only after it's already noisy. we should surface a short-window probe for slab-throttle events (5s) to trigger mitigations faster.

alex: agreed. for immediate mitigations: 1) pin tenant-819 to soft-isolation pool, 2) increase per-tenant kvcache limit, 3) enable short-window alert. i can run the pin now if folks +1.

sara: +1 to pin. but we need a rollback plan if pinning causes capacity pressure elsewhere. propose: pin with temporary burst-credit 0.5 and auto-unpin after 15m if no recurrence. low risk and quick.

lina: we should also try an ingress policer on the shard NIC to smooth RX bursts. sample eBPF rule I used in prod: 
```
# drop if per-tenant rate > 500 req/s for 2s window
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip u32 match ip dst 0/0 flowid 1:1 
    police rate 500kburst 10k mtu 64 drop
```
This reduced slab churn last month.

kai: routing fallback plan: add tenant-819 to dedicated-fallback group and set route weight 0.8 -> ded-pool, 0.2 -> shared during canary. cheap to revert.

ben: I'll push a quick telemetry change: new probe event "slab_throttle_short" aggregation window 5s + instant slack alert. will tag ops-bot.

ops-bot: ALERT: GPU_SLAB_THROTTLE eu-west1 spike detected (tenant: candidate suspects: tenant-819) — count=1287 window=180s — severity=warning

alex: done pinning tenant-819 to soft-isolation (dedicated-fallback applied). watching metrics.

sara: early numbers look better — slab-throttle count falling. keeping pinned for 15m then reevaluate.

lina: follow-up ask: can we add per-tenant kvcache backpressure instead of global evictions? long term fix: per-slab loaning + lease to avoid full-scan invalidations. filing infra-tech-debt ticket.

kai: also track cost delta — dedicated routing increases unit cost but buys latency SLO. put cost estimate in ticket.

ben: telemetryrc: added probe and a dashboard panel for 5s slab spikes. will alert page if >100/s for 30s.

alex: thanks all. reopening if it flares. will post postmortem if we need an RCA. :thumbsup:
